General Hospital Discharge Policy

This document outlines the standard policies and procedures governing the discharge of patients from Riverside General Hospital (a fictional institution created for illustrative purposes). All content is synthetic and for educational use only.

Discharge Eligibility Criteria:
Patients are eligible for discharge when the attending physician determines that: the patient's vital signs are stable and within acceptable ranges, the patient's pain is adequately controlled with oral medications, the patient is able to safely perform basic activities of daily living or has appropriate home support, the patient demonstrates understanding of discharge instructions, and necessary follow-up care arrangements have been made.

Discharge Planning Process:
Discharge planning begins at the time of hospital admission for elective procedures and immediately upon stabilization for urgent cases. The discharge planning team includes the attending physician, case manager or social worker, nursing staff, and physical and occupational therapists as appropriate. The team works collaboratively to identify the patient's post-discharge needs, arrange necessary services, and ensure the patient and caregivers are prepared.

Patient Education Prior to Discharge:
Before leaving the hospital, every patient will receive verbal and written instructions covering: current medical condition and procedure performed, medications prescribed (names, doses, frequency, and purpose), activity restrictions and guidelines, wound care instructions if applicable, diet and nutrition guidance, follow-up appointment information, and instructions on when to call the doctor or return to the hospital.

Discharge Destination Planning:
Patients may be discharged to their home, a skilled nursing facility, an inpatient rehabilitation facility, or another level of care depending on their functional status and support needs. Home health services (including nursing visits, physical therapy, and occupational therapy) may be arranged if the patient requires ongoing professional care at home. The case manager coordinates placement and insurance authorization as needed.

Medication Reconciliation:
A complete medication reconciliation is performed at discharge. All new prescriptions are reviewed for accuracy, interactions, and alignment with the patient's discharge diagnoses. Patients are educated about each new medication, including any newly prescribed pain medications, blood thinners, or antibiotics. A printed medication list is provided to the patient and, with consent, to the designated caregiver.

Transportation Requirements:
Patients cannot be discharged in a vehicle they are driving themselves if: they have received general anesthesia within the past 24 hours, they are taking opioid pain medications, or they have been advised not to drive by their care team. Patients must arrange for a responsible adult to drive them home. Taxis, ride-share services, and public transportation are acceptable when accompanied by a responsible adult.

Patient Rights at Discharge:
Patients have the right to refuse discharge, though this is handled through a formal review process. Patients who are members of a managed care plan must comply with plan requirements regarding discharge destination and follow-up care. If a patient believes they are being discharged prematurely, they may request a review through the hospital's patient advocate or the appropriate state oversight body.

Post-Discharge Follow-Up by the Hospital:
Riverside General Hospital (fictional) conducts post-discharge follow-up calls within 48–72 hours for all surgical patients and patients discharged on new anticoagulant or pain medications. These calls serve to confirm the patient arrived home safely, answer questions about medications or instructions, and ensure follow-up appointments are scheduled. Patients experiencing difficulty are directed to appropriate resources or instructed to return for evaluation.

Compliance and Documentation:
All discharge instructions are documented in the patient's electronic health record. Patients and caregivers are asked to sign a discharge instruction acknowledgment form confirming they received and understood the instructions. A copy of discharge instructions is provided to the patient and uploaded to the patient portal if available.
